title: Unique residue-map lifting from a perfect-residue Cohen ring
statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a Cohen ring of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Write $K=A/pA$, and suppose $K$ is perfect, meaning that $x\mapsto x^p$ is bijective on $K$. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $j:K\to R/\mathfrak m$ be a field homomorphism. There is a unique local ring homomorphism $f:A\to R$ whose induced residue map is $j$, that is, $q_R f=j q_A$, where $q_R:R\to R/\mathfrak m$ and $q_A:A\to K$ are the quotient maps. Local means $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=pA$.

source.place: Exposé IV Theorem 4.1.8(i) with I the maximal ideal, and 4.1.9 (perfect residue implies vanishing differentials), printed pp.57–58; uniqueness used in 4.3.5.

proof.text: Set $k_R=R/\mathfrak m$. The Cohen-ring definition [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] gives $\ker q_A=pA$ and makes $K$ a field. The field map $j$ is injective: a nonzero kernel element would give $j(1)=0$. Since $p=0$ in $K$, also $p=0$ in $k_R$, hence $p_R\in\mathfrak m$. Begin with $h_1=j q_A:A\to R/\mathfrak m$. We construct maps $h_n:A\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ for $n\ge1$, compatible with the quotient projections and with this $h_1$.

source.place: Exposé IV 4.1.7–4.1.8(i), printed p.57; initial residue map.

proof.text: Suppose $h_n$ is constructed. Put $D=R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and $J=\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subset D$. Then $D/J\cong R/\mathfrak m^n$ canonically, $J^2=0$ because $2n\ge n+1$, and $p^{n+1}=0$ in $D$ because $p_R\in\mathfrak m$. As a ring map, $h_n$ kills $p^{n+1}A$, so it induces $\bar h_n:A/p^{n+1}A\to D/J$. Apply the explicit square-zero lifting clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] with exponent $n+1$, ring $D$, ideal $J$ and map $\bar h_n$. Precomposing its lift with $A\to A/p^{n+1}A$ gives $h_{n+1}$ whose reduction is $h_n$. Recursive choice therefore gives the required compatible sequence.

source.place: Tag 0329, lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth; Tag 032A, theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, positive-residue-characteristic lifting paragraph.

proof.text: For each $a\in A$, the compatible tuple $(h_n(a))_{n\ge1}$ is an element of $\varprojlim_n R/\mathfrak m^n$. By [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] it comes from exactly one element $f(a)\in R$. The coordinate maps $h_n$ preserve $0,1,+,\cdot$; injectivity of the completion map therefore shows that $f$ preserves these operations, so $f$ is a ring homomorphism. Its first coordinate gives $q_R f=j q_A$. Consequently $f(a)\in\mathfrak m$ if and only if $j(q_A(a))=0$, if and only if $q_A(a)=0$, if and only if $a\in pA$. This proves locality as well as existence.

source.place: Tag 0317, definition-complete; Tag 032A, theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, inverse-limit assembly.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $f,g:A\to R$ both have residue map $j$. Inductively prove $f(a)-g(a)\in\mathfrak m^n$ for every $a$ and every $n\ge1$; the base is their residue equality. For the induction step, perfectness of $K$ lets us choose $b,c\in A$ with $a=b^p+pc$: lift a $p$th root of $q_A(a)$ to $b$, and use $\ker q_A=pA$. Write $d=f(b)-g(b)\in\mathfrak m^n$. Expanding $(g(b)+d)^p-g(b)^p$, its term linear in $d$ is $p_R g(b)^{p-1}d\in\mathfrak m^{n+1}$; each term of degree at least two in $d$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{2n}\subseteq\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Also $p_R(f(c)-g(c))\in\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Thus $f(a)-g(a)=f(b)^p-g(b)^p+p_R(f(c)-g(c))$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, completing the induction.

source.place: Exposé IV 4.1.8(i) and 4.1.9, printed pp.57–58; agent-written binomial verification of the perfect-residue uniqueness assertion.

proof.text: By the separatedness included in [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\bigcap_{n\ge1}\mathfrak m^n=0$. The preceding congruences give $f(a)=g(a)$ for every $a\in A$, hence $f=g$. Together with the constructed local lift this proves the stated existence and uniqueness.

It changes only the item, adds no new nodes and has a Q81 review section. The statement matches ILO IV 4.1.8(i) with I = m and u = j∘q_A, which is local because j is injective and ker q_A = pA, together with 4.1.9 (Ω¹_K = 0 iff K perfect) for uniqueness. It is unchanged, with nothing added or dropped. Step 1 is correct: K is a field, j is injective and p_R lies in m. Step 2: the explicit square-zero clause of lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth (reviewed by L) is applied with exponent n+1, D = R/m^{n+1} and J = m^n/m^{n+1}. J² = 0 because n ≥ 1, p^{n+1}D = 0, and h_n kills p^{n+1}, so every hypothesis holds. Step 3 assembles f by the bijectivity in the completeness definition, and the locality equivalence is correct. Step 4 is a binomial induction, with a = b^p + pc from Frobenius surjectivity; the term linear in d lies in m^{n+1} and the higher terms in m^{2n}. Step 5 uses ∩m^n = 0. I tested R a field, R = A, R = A/p^e, p = 2 with n = 1, p zero or a zero divisor in R, and a proper extension j. No duplicate exists: cohen-ring-lift-complete-local needs a residue isomorphism and gives existence only, and the coefficient-ring and presentation nodes state different things. The citer, equivariant-cohen-coefficient-lift step 2, uses exactly the stated existence and uniqueness. I accept the tool_use of the generic sk-thm-p1 Stacks 0329 lifting node. No SGA source is used.
